editorial:
You meet Duncan, a tired hitman counting down to retirement, but his old company decides he is worth more dead than alive. Instead of fading away, he gets pulled into a bloody showdown with a flashy crew of younger killers. The movie mixes dark humor, wild action, and a gritty comic-book style, so you know right away it is not a quiet drama. Mads Mikkelsen gives Duncan a calm, dangerous edge, while the villains bring loud energy and bad intentions. It feels like a revenge story with a strange heart, especially when Duncan connects with a lonely neighbor who has her own pain. The tone is rough, flashy, and sometimes over the top, but that is part of the fun.

The action scenes are fast and brutal, with strong stunt work and a cool winter look. Mikkelsen carries the movie well, and the younger killers keep things unpredictable. On the downside, the humor can be crude, the violence is heavy, and some characters feel cartoonish. If you like stylish revenge movies and do not mind blood, you will probably have a good time.
endingExplained: In the final act, Duncan learns the hit on him was tied to a bigger plan involving his retirement payout and the younger assassins. He fights through the crew, survives the ambush, and turns the tables on the people who ordered his death. The last scenes show him walking away from the chaos with his freedom, while the remaining threat is handled. You see that his quiet retirement was never going to be easy, but he proves he is still the most dangerous person in the room.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stylish revenge movies with dark humor and heavy action.
